A Memorable Fine Dining Journey in Saigon
Mar 2026 • Couples
Akuna is easily one of the most impressive dining experiences I’ve had in Saigon so far. It’s the kind of place you go to not just for a meal, but for the full journey.

The tasting menu is thoughtfully designed, with multiple courses that flow really well from start to finish. Nothing feels random — every dish has its place and builds on the experience. Flavours are bold yet refined, with a strong umami profile and a clear sense of creativity behind each plate.

What I really enjoyed is how the food reflects the chef’s personality and ideas. It’s not just about technique, but also about storytelling and emotion in the dishes.

Service also stands out. The team is confident, attentive without being overbearing, and communicates very well in English. They make you feel comfortable, keep the experience relaxed, and guide you through the meal at a very natural pace.

The space itself is calm and intimate, perfect for a special occasion or a proper sit-down dinner where you can really slow down and enjoy.

Overall, it feels worth the price for what you get. Definitely a place I’d come back to, and one I’d recommend if you’re looking for something memorable in Saigon.

Akuna- a well deserved Michelin star
May 2025 • Friends
Akuna 
Akuna deserves its 1-star Michelin rating—a perfect example of modern fine dining. My first encounter with this style was at Commis, a 2-star Michelin near Berkeley, where a salad resembling jello burst with the fresh flavors of a garden. Akuna nails this innovative approach, using modern techniques to surprise with unexpected presentations while preserving authentic tastes and aromas, or cleverly subverting them with familiar-looking dishes that taste entirely new.
Compared to East, where Ngo Thanh Hoa’s modern cooking earns a solid 4 stars, Akuna shines brighter with a full 5-star experience. I’ll definitely be back.
One note: the early courses leaned heavily on acidity, which unsettled my empty stomach. I requested bread and butter to balance it out. If you have a sensitive stomach or arrive hungry, consider informing the kitchen in advance.

Very bad food experience in Vietnam
Jan 2025 • Family
A Waste of Money – A Disappointing Michelin Experience at Akuna

My family and I ended an otherwise wonderful vacation with what we thought would be a memorable dinner at Akuna. With its high rating of 4.5 stars and a Michelin star, we believed the 30 million dong would be well spent. Unfortunately, we were sorely disappointed, and it turned out to be the worst dining experience we’ve had.

I only read the reviews after our visit, and the negative comments perfectly describe what we experienced. My wife and son both had upset stomachs all night after the meal, which only added to our frustration. I truly don’t understand how Akuna earned a Michelin star with so many poor reviews and such bad food.

As many other one- and two-star reviews point out, the food lacked any real character and didn’t have the distinct flavors we were expecting. It felt like they were trying to combine all the tastes at once, without any of them standing out in a positive way.

A good example of this was the dish "Confit Pork Jowl, Fremantle Octopus, Pickled Straw Mushrooms, White Kombu, Choko Shoots, Fish Sauce." While the confit pork jowl was tasty, it was cooked in fish sauce, which completely overwhelmed the natural flavors with a burnt fish sauce taste. To enjoy the pork, we had to remove the skin and fat, just to find the actual good flavor.

The pickled mushrooms were fine, but after reading about them online, I discovered that they can be quite harsh on the digestive system — not exactly something I’d expect from a Michelin restaurant. The Fremantle octopus didn’t look very appetizing alongside the pork and had a rubbery texture, which was confusing when paired with the soft pork.

The white kombu, also known as the "fifth taste" or umami, was almost impossible to taste because the burnt fish sauce completely dominated everything. 
The choko shoots, which tasted like beans, were again undetectable due to the overpowering fish sauce.
 I really don’t understand why they used fish sauce in a dish that already had umami ingredients and good pork flavour.

We also ordered extra truffle for 1.4 million dong, but it was truly a waste of money. The truffle was grated and drowned in a mix of oysters, sea cucumber, egg, samphire, and pork fond. All the potential flavors were lost due to the unbalanced combination, and the good taste was completely absent, and so was the money.

All in all, it was a truly disappointing experience, and I can’t understand how Akuna received a Michelin star. It was a waste of money and time, and we won’t be returning ever.

I’m Horribly Confused
Nov 2024 • Couples
I will give credit where it is due, the presentation of each meal was excellent and the staff were lovely, however i attend dinner to enjoy my food and enjoy i did not. Dinner started with a palate cleanser of biblical proportion, my wife was left looking confused by the 3 options served upon what i can only describe as a deconstructed vietnamese hat. 
The first course was confusing to look at, however the best tasting of the night, an egg yolk presented in it’s shell, with caviar and cream fraiche, tasty, yes, confusing, also yes. 

Our second course we continued with perhaps a little hesitation.

But our third course, all hope was lost as they rolled out the sliced sea cucumber (the texture is as you would expect) and i received the extras from my wife as she believed firmly, sea cucumber belong at the bottom of the ocean.

Our optimism returned with back to back hits! A palate cleanser of damper with Vegemite and goats cheese (we may be biased as Australians but these did help Akuna’s case) and confit pork jowl to back it up, also quite enjoyable.

As we believed this would improve the flavour we paid the extra 2 million dong for some truffle shavings on our next course (this was very aesthetic as they shave it in front of you) however aesthetic was as far is at went, as we quickly realised there was no flavour to the truffle, at all. The rest of the meal, mouse deer and fermented yabbi was tough and very bland. 

The palate cleanser for dessert was i believe the pièce de résistance, a biscuit resembling a goldfish, filled with a jam that was overpowered by the mediocre texture and taste of the biscuit, reminding me only of the soggy bit of biscuit that has fallen into the bottom of your tea as you dip your scotch finger into it at 11 at night. 

Our dessert, was a trio of jelly and a sliced up melon, the melon was fine, you could run your car on the jelly. Nothing to write home about.

Last dessert came out in 2 baskets hung on a yolk, at this point, we were ready to go and this did not improve the mood as much as one might hope. 

The whole experience was confusing and the friendly staff can only make it so bearable when you spend 12 million dong to eat good food and realise the pho from lunch could have comfortably replaced any of these courses.

Mar 2024 • Friends
I just had a very delicious and interesting experience at Akuna. The space is very luxurious and cozy, with tables and chairs arranged far enough apart for privacy. There is a very large open table in the middle to observe the chefs preparing food. I tried the 4-course dinner, which did not include petit four appetizers, bread, and petit four dessert. Every dish is very meticulous, combining many fresh and unique ingredients but very suitable for my taste. I really like the steamed eggs here, they melt in my mouth. The same goes for the tuna belly sashimi, greasy. This was also the first time I tried porcupine meat, the meat was soft and succulent. The staff are very nice, taking care of your table quite thoughtfully. Worthy of a 10/10 experience!
